headline: High risk: shared filesystem plus broad shell/write privileges make prompt injection, data leakage, and cascading errors plausible by default.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Cursor ingests workspace files, open buffers, clipboard, and MCP outputs; Open Interpreter can read/write the whole filesystem and clipboard. Their shared filesystem bridge makes attacker-controlled content from one agent plausibly parsed by the other as instructions, though this is not as direct as a raw web-content pipeline.
conditions: IF either agent writes untrusted text into a shared workspace file and the other agent reads it as instructions, injection is possible.
IF MCP or clipboard is used to pass content between the agents, prompt injection risk increases.
mitigations: Separate workspaces per agent.
Disable clipboard-based handoff between agents.
Require a human review step before one agent consumes the other's file output.
Use read-only mounts for shared artifacts.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to inter-agent files.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Both agents can read local files and have broad network egress; Cursor explicitly touches open files and clipboard, while Open Interpreter can access anything reachable on the local machine. In a shared filesystem setup, sensitive local data can flow into either agent and then out through model-provider/API calls, creating a realistic exfiltration path by default.
conditions: IF sensitive files are present in the shared workspace, either agent can ingest them.
IF either agent sends context to a remote model provider, those files may leave the local machine.
mitigations: Remove secrets from the shared workspace.
Run one agent at a time on sensitive projects.
Disable network egress for the less-trusted agent.
Use separate OS users or containers.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention filters.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents have unrestricted filesystem write, shell execution, and git-state modification, and both share state via the filesystem. Without locking, concurrent edits can overwrite files or corrupt git state; the overlap is broad and the blast radius can include irreversible repository damage.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same repo or directory concurrently, write conflicts can occur.
IF either agent auto-runs shell commands while the other is editing the same files, corruption risk rises.
mitigations: Assign each agent a separate checkout.
Pause one agent before the other writes.
Use git worktrees or branches per agent.
Turn off auto-run/Yolo mode during concurrent work.
requires-engineering: add file locks around shared mutable paths.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Cursor can emit code, patches, and file edits that Open Interpreter can then act on with shell and filesystem authority. Because Open Interpreter can execute arbitrary code as the user and Cursor can use MCP/tool loops, a mistaken or malicious output from one can cascade into destructive actions by the other without strong verification.
conditions: IF Open Interpreter consumes Cursor-generated commands or patches without verification, errors can propagate into execution.
IF Cursor writes instructions that Open Interpreter treats as authoritative, downstream actions may be taken automatically.
mitigations: Require manual approval before execution.
Have a human verify patches before running them.
Limit Open Interpreter to read-only mode for review tasks.
Use a checklist for command provenance.
requires-engineering: add schema validation for inter-agent handoffs.

E_compliance.rationale: Cursor handles open files and clipboard contents, while Open Interpreter can access anything reachable on the local machine. If regulated data is present locally, both agents may process it under different logging, retention, or provider-routing behaviors; the profiles do not document matching compliance controls, so the mismatch is plausible but not proven.
conditions: IF regulated data is stored on the local machine, both agents may process it.
IF their provider or retention settings differ, compliance obligations may diverge.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the shared workspace.
Use a dedicated compliant environment.
Review provider and retention settings for both agents.
Disable clipboard transfer for regulated content.
requires-engineering: document and enforce a common data-handling policy.
